newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks hit third consecutive record close.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks hit third consecutive record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks marched to a record high close for the third consecutive day, boosted by a positive outlook for lending rates and the potential impact of that scenario on the market's chief sectors, brokers said. "We haven't seen any visible signs of inflation, any sign of a rise in interest rates," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "In the U.S., Hong Kong and China everything seems to be going our way."
The Hang Seng Index held onto 110.23 points to set a new record close of 13,167.16, after trading 172.22 points up at a new intraday high of 13,229.15 early in the day.
"The market is up on the long bond and liquidity," said Wong.

The yield on the U.S. 30-year treasury bond has continued to trend at low levels, closing Tuesday trading in New York down at 6.44 percent against 6.47 percent at Monday's close, which brokers said pointed to continued low, steady interest rates till next year.
Turnover soared to HK$12.29 billion, substantially up on Tuesday's HK$10.48 billion. It is has only been higher once this year-- at HK$12.61 billion on February 7.
Volatility has been low in this rally, despite the increase in derivatives issued and trading in the market, Wong said.

Ted Chen, technical analyst at Technical Data Inc, said from a statistical viewpoint the index's most recent advance had been quite steady. He said he was cautiously optimistic on the near term outlook.
"The average duration of an intermediate rally in Hong Kong had been four months or 120 days," said Chen. "The current rally started in early August and will have matured by early December."
He added: "This is not the end of the rally, but a time to be more cautious."
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was brisk. The November contract put on 140 points to close at 13,195, a 28-point premium to the cash market, on trade of 18,650 contracts.
Interest rate sensitive property stocks led the market, followed closely by utility shares.
Henderson Land rose HK$1.50 to close at HK$74.75 after touching a new all time high of HK$75.25. Buoyed by continued interest in China plays, Kerry Properties added HK$1.40 to HK$22.65.
HongKong Telecom put on HK$0.20 to HK$13.75.
